chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the captive of the Kurds when they wage war, and whoever of the polytheists wages war, is their marriage permissible and their purchase? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Are the captives of the Kurds permissible for marriage and purchase according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of marrying and enslaving captives from the Kurds and other polytheists who engage in hostilities, affirming their status as *milk al-yamin* (those owned by the right). It highlights the Shia juristic view that specific tribal or religious groups engaged in war against the Muslim community are subject to these rulings, provided they are not from the People of the Book in a manner that precludes it. The narration underscores the practical application of captives' status in classical Islamic law regarding marriage contracts and ownership.
